plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before its leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in East Asia for ornamental use and for its sour fruit, which is pickled or made into liqueur.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea, and temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are celebrated in East Asia as a symbol of perseverance because they bloom in the cold, often while snow is still on the ground, and they traditionally herald spring before cherry blossoms.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It carpets woodlands and gardens, often emerging through lingering snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Europe, from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce a natural antifreeze-like protein that helps them survive freezing, and the compound galantamine from related plants is used in medicine for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An evergreen Australian tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, golden, ball-shaped flower clusters with a sweet fragrance. Its sickle-shaped leaves are actually flattened leaf stalks called phyllodes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in Australia (July to October), with related wattles and acacias flowering in other months across the continent
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring in the Southern Hemisphere.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up leafless stalks topped with clusters of large, fragrant, trumpet-shaped flowers. The strap-like leaves appear after flowering and die back in summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn in the Southern Hemisphere (February to April)
plants.location: Western Cape of South Africa; naturalized in Australia, California, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: The common name 'naked lady' comes from the way the flower stalks emerge from bare ground without any leaves, often after the first autumn rains or heat.
